items.name: Apple Watch Ultra 2
items.summary: Apple's most capable watch: dual-frequency GPS, a 3,000-nit display, a programmable Action button and recreational dive-computer features. It shows how far smartwatches have moved into tool-watch territory.

items.name: Royal Oak "Jumbo" Extra-Thin
items.summary: The closest modern descendant of the 1972 original: 39 mm, extra-thin, "Petite Tapisserie" dial and the octagonal bezel with eight exposed screws that changed luxury forever. Its 2012 update (with the AP logo at 6 o'clock) is sometimes cited as the launch date; the reference itself dates to 2000.

items.name: F-91W
items.summary: Possibly the best-selling watch in history: light, accurate, nearly indestructible and costs about as much as lunch. A design classic that every collector should understand.

items.name: G-Shock DW-5000C
items.milestone: The first G-Shock: a module floating inside a shock-absorbing case

case.material: Resin over a floating module, stainless steel screw-back

items.summary: The first G-Shock, launched in April 1983. Kikuo Ibe's brief was a single line: "a durable watch that would not break even if dropped". The module floats inside a hollow, shock-absorbing resin case. Sources disagree on its original depth rating (100 m or 200 m), so it is not stated here.

items.name: G-Shock DW-5000R "Origin Revival"
items.milestone: A standard-issue re-creation of the 1983 original

case.material: Bio-based resin bezel over stainless steel case, screw-lock back

items.summary: A standard-issue (non-limited) re-creation of the 1983 DW-5000C, made at Yamagata Casio in Japan, with the screw-lock steel case of the original and a bio-based resin band and bezel.

items.name: G-Shock DW-5040PG "Recrystallized"
items.milestone: 40th anniversary: recrystallised, hardened steel

case.material: Resin; recrystallised, deep-layer-hardened stainless steel back, buckle and loop

items.summary: A 40th-anniversary limited edition from the Recrystallized series (2023): the original DW-5000 design, with a case back, buckle and loop in steel treated by recrystallisation and deep-layer hardening.

items.name: G-Shock DW-5200C
items.milestone: The near-identical successor that broke through in the US
items.summary: A near-identical successor to the DW-5000C, released in 1984, the year a US television advert that used the watch as a hockey puck helped turn G-Shock into a hit.

items.name: G-Shock DW-5500C
items.milestone: First Mud Resist G-Shock
items.summary: Casio's first Mud Resist G-Shock, using two-tone moulding to seal the square case against mud and dust: the ancestor of the later Mudman line.

items.name: G-Shock DW-5600E
items.milestone: EL backlight and module 3229
items.summary: The square descendant of Kikuo Ibe's original 1983 G-Shock, introduced in 1996 to replace the DW-5600C with an EL backlight and module 3229. A suspended module and resin armour make it one of the toughest watches you can buy, at any price.

items.name: G-Shock DW-5600C
items.milestone: The first "5600": the definitive square shape
items.summary: The first "5600", the shape that became the definitive square G-Shock. It sold for nine years until the EL-backlit DW-5600E replaced it in 1996; the module changed from 691 to 901 around 1989 or 1990, depending on the source.

items.name: G-Shock GMW-B5000D "Full Metal"
items.milestone: First full-metal square, with Bluetooth
items.summary: The first full-metal 5000-series G-Shock, released in Japan in April 2018 for the 35th anniversary: the 1983 shape rebuilt in steel with resin shock absorbers between case and bezel, solar power, radio sync and Bluetooth.

items.name: G-Shock GW-B5600
items.milestone: Full-metal functions in a lightweight resin case
items.summary: The resin twin of the full-metal GMW-B5000: the same solar, Multi-Band 6 and Bluetooth functions in the classic lightweight 5600 case, announced in Japan in October 2018.

items.name: G-Shock GW-M5610
items.milestone: Solar and atomic radio sync for an everyday price
items.summary: The square that never needs setting or a battery change: solar-charged and synchronised by radio with atomic clocks. Its GW-M5600 predecessor launched in 2008; the exact debut year of the 5610 is not confirmed by the sources, so it is not stated here.

items.name: G-Shock GW-5000
items.milestone: Made in Japan with a screw-back, solar power and radio sync

case.material: Resin with stainless steel case and screw-back (DLC)

items.summary: A made-in-Japan homage to the 1983 original, with a screw-lock back, solar power and radio sync. It is held in the Victoria and Albert Museum's collection as a 2009 design, and was succeeded by the GW-5000U.

items.name: G-Shock GW-5000U
items.milestone: Module 3495 brings a full auto LED backlight

case.material: Resin with stainless steel case and screw-back (DLC)

items.summary: The updated, made-in-Japan GW-5000: the new module 3495 adds a full auto LED backlight with adjustable afterglow and an adjustable date format, while keeping the screw-back, solar charging and Multi-Band 6.

items.name: Promaster Diver
items.summary: An ISO-rated, light-powered diver that never needs a battery change in normal use. Arguably the most practical dive watch you can buy for the money.

items.name: fēnix 8
items.summary: A multisport flagship with AMOLED or solar MIP displays, offline maps, a built-in flashlight and battery life measured in weeks rather than hours.

items.name: "Snowflake"
items.summary: A dial textured like wind-blown snow around Shiojiri, a feather-light titanium case and the gliding seconds hand of Spring Drive. Many collectors' gateway to Grand Seiko.

items.name: Khaki Field Mechanical
items.summary: A hand-wound field watch with roots in Hamilton's military pieces. With an 80-hour power reserve and a legible 12/24-hour dial, it is a perfect introduction to the ritual of winding.

items.name: Janata
items.summary: "Janata" means "the people". Simple, hand-wound and built to last, it was the everyday watch of millions in India and is now a beloved collectible and vintage starting point.

items.name: Speedmaster Professional Moonwatch
items.summary: Flight-qualified by NASA in 1965 and worn on the Moon in 1969. The current version keeps the hand-wound chronograph and hesalite crystal but adds the Master Chronometer calibre 3861.

items.name: Nautilus
items.caliber: Patek Philippe 324 S C (26-330 S C in the final years)
items.summary: Gérald Genta's porthole-inspired design (1976) in its most coveted modern form. Its discontinuation made it a symbol of the secondary-market boom.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: Ceramic bezel and Super Case come to the no-date
items.summary: The modern no-date Submariner: Cerachrom bezel, Super Case and the calibre 3130 with a blue Parachrom hairspring.

items.name: Submariner Date
items.milestone: Cerachrom ceramic bezel and the thick-lugged Super Case
items.summary: The first Submariner Date with a Cerachrom ceramic bezel, a Maxi dial and thick-lugged "Super Case". It kept the calibre 3135 and a 40 mm diameter.

items.name: Submariner Date "Hulk"
items.milestone: "Hulk": green dial and green ceramic bezel
items.summary: A green sunburst dial matched with a green Cerachrom bezel in the 40 mm Super Case. Its discontinuation in 2020 made it a modern collectible.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: 41 mm, slimmer lugs and the 70-hour calibre 3230
items.summary: The no-date Submariner, the purest form of the dive watch that has defined the genre since 1953. The 2020 generation grew to 41 mm and gained the 70-hour calibre 3230.

items.name: Submariner Date
items.milestone: 41 mm Submariner Date with the 70-hour calibre 3235
items.summary: The current Submariner Date: 41 mm with slimmer lugs, the 70-hour calibre 3235 with Chronergy escapement, and a Glidelock clasp for tool-free adjustment.

items.name: Submariner Date "Starbucks"
items.milestone: "Starbucks": green ceramic bezel over a black dial
items.summary: A green Cerachrom bezel over a black dial in the 41 mm case with the 70-hour calibre 3235. Collectors nicknamed it "Starbucks"; it succeeded both the Kermit and the Hulk.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: The no-date returns with sapphire and 904L steel
items.summary: The no-date Submariner reborn for the modern era: sapphire crystal, 904L steel and the calibre 3000. Unlike its date sibling it was not chronometer-certified.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: Calibre 3130; the last no-date with an aluminium bezel
items.summary: The 14060 updated with the calibre 3130, later chronometer-certified and with an engraved rehaut. It was the last no-date Submariner with an aluminium bezel; sources date its end to 2009 or 2012.

items.name: Submariner Date
items.milestone: Calibre 3135: the classic Submariner Date for two decades
items.summary: For two decades the definitive Submariner Date: calibre 3135, an aluminium bezel insert and the classic slim-lug 40 mm case. Many collectors consider it the last "traditional" Submariner.

items.name: Submariner Date "Kermit"
items.milestone: The 50th-anniversary "Kermit": the first green bezel
items.summary: Launched for the Submariner's 50th anniversary as the first Submariner with a green bezel: a green aluminium insert over a black dial. Early "Flat 4" bezels are especially sought after.

items.name: Submariner Date
items.milestone: First Submariner with a date and Cyclops lens
items.summary: The first Submariner with a date and Cyclops magnifier, launching the line that leads to today's Submariner Date. Early dials carry the prized red "Submariner" script. Sources give its launch as 1967 or 1969.

items.name: Submariner Date
items.milestone: Sapphire crystal, 300 m and a quickset date
items.summary: The transitional Submariner Date: sapphire crystal, 300 m water resistance (still the standard today), a quickset date and a high-beat calibre 3035. Matte dials gave way to glossy dials with white-gold surrounds in the mid-1980s.

items.name: Submariner Date "Triple Zero"
items.milestone: The switch to 904L steel
items.summary: A very short-lived reference marking Rolex's switch to 904L steel; otherwise essentially a 16800. Sources describe production lasting from about nine months to two years.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: Small 6 mm crown and the new calibre 1530
items.summary: A small-crown Submariner with a 6 mm crown and the calibre 1530, bridging the first generation and the crown-guard era. Sources disagree on its depth rating (100 m or 200 m) and on its exact production years, so neither is stated here.

items.name: Submariner "Big Crown"
items.milestone: Short-lived big-crown model with the calibre 1530
items.summary: A short-lived, rare reference: effectively the 6200/6538 big-crown architecture updated with the calibre 1530.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: First with crown guards, a 40 mm case and chronometer certification
items.summary: The first Submariner with crown guards and a 40 mm case, and the first chronometer-certified Submariner. The guards evolved from square to pointed to rounded. Sources give the end of production as 1978, 1979 or 1980.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: The non-chronometer workhorse, made for almost three decades
items.summary: The non-chronometer sibling of the 5512 and one of Rolex's longest-running references, produced for almost three decades. It is the classic vintage Submariner and the basis of the military MilSub.

items.name: Submariner "MilSub"
items.milestone: Military issue: sword hands, fixed bars and tritium
items.summary: Made for the British Ministry of Defence: sword hands, a full-graduation bezel, fixed spring bars and a circled T for tritium on the dial. Only about 1,200 to 1,250 were delivered, making it one of the rarest Submariners.

items.name: Submariner "Big Crown"
items.milestone: First 200 m Submariner, with an 8 mm "big crown"
items.summary: The first 200 m Submariner, with an 8 mm "big crown" and an Explorer-style 3-6-9 dial; it did not yet carry the Submariner name on the dial. Sources date its launch between 1953 and 1955, and it was succeeded by the 5510 in 1958.

items.name: Submariner (first series)
items.milestone: The first Submariner: 37 mm, 100 m, a rotating timing bezel
items.summary: The first Submariner, shown at the 1954 Basel fair and rated to 100 m. A 37 mm case, small unprotected crown and straight pencil hands; whether the 6204 or the near-identical 6205 came first is still debated.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: A near twin of the 6204, still without a depth rating on the dial
items.summary: A near twin of the 6204 with the same A260 movement and 37 mm case, and still no depth rating on the dial. In 1955 it evolved into the 6536.

items.name: Submariner
items.milestone: Upgraded to the full-rotor calibre 1030
items.summary: The small-crown successor to the 6205, upgraded to the full-rotor calibre 1030; a chronometer version was sold as the 6536/1. Most sources rate it to 100 m, and its exact launch year (1955 or 1956) varies between them.

items.name: Submariner "Big Crown"
items.milestone: The big-crown 200 m reference linked to Dr. No
items.summary: The big-crown, 200 m reference famously associated with Sean Connery in Dr. No (1962), although some sources attribute the film watch to a 6536. Today it is among the most valuable Submariners at auction.

items.name: Presage "Cocktail Time"
items.summary: A textured, cocktail-inspired sunburst dial that punches far above its price, and a common recommendation for a first dressy automatic.

items.name: SKX007
items.summary: The definitive affordable ISO-rated dive watch for more than two decades, and the starting point of the modding scene. Its 4 o'clock crown and legible dial are textbook tool-watch design.

items.name: PRX Powermatic 80
items.summary: A 1970s-style integrated bracelet watch with a "Clous de Paris" waffle dial and an 80-hour power reserve, giving the sports-luxury look at a fraction of the price.

items.name: Black Bay Fifty-Eight
items.summary: A vintage-proportioned 39 mm diver inspired by Tudor's 1958 references, with a 70-hour in-house movement. It turned Tudor into a brand enthusiasts buy for its own sake.
